utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I was informed that the Stanisic Defence wanted to address the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Very briefly, if I may, just on the issue of Mr. Stanisic being brought to court. Yesterday he was picked at 1.00 p.m. from the detention centre and arrived at the court at approximately 1.15, which meant he has to sit and wait for one hour. And then he was brought back to the detention centre and arrived at 8.00 p.m. I would just respectfully ask that Your Honours might intervene at some stage if it becomes necessary. Mr. Stanisic is, as Your Honours knows, under full therapy, including antibiotics, morphine, and also, at present, a therapy dealing with his thrombosis issues. And being brought to court an hour earlier puts an extra strain on his ability to be able to focus on the proceedings, and I'd ask that his health issues are given some consideration when it comes to his transport to the court. I think he was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I think you would like us to do is to intervene and to take care that the transportation time is as little as possible, and the waiting time. That's understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll get in touch with the Registrar. You may be aware that it most likely is a matter of co-ordination also with the Dutch authorities. First of all, it's now on the record. But the Chamber will further monitor what is done, and we'll liaise with the Registrar. Any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move into closed session. And could the witness be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in closed session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness DST-040. Please be seated. I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday. And Mr. Jordash will now continue his examination-in-chief. Mr. Jordash, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have on the screen, please, 1D05046.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Would you have a look at the map on the screen, Mr. Witness, and confirm that these are some of the main areas which your testimony will cover, or does cover.

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I tendered this as an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be D422, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D422 is admitted into evidence. No need to have it under seal, I take it, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Witness, the evidence we've just gone through, your statement, chart of exhibits, the proofing note, and the map, are now evidence before the Court, so we don't need to repeat what's contained within. I'll now take you through some of your evidence to clarify and to elaborate. You follow me?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. A witness in this case, Mr. DST-040, described you as the deputy of the Ilok Police Station in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sorry, isn't this DST-040?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think yes, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It wasn't --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were addressing Witness DST-040 and told him that a witness in this case described him as the deputy of the Ilok Police Station.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, it wasn't very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me try that again.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: DST-040, which is you, as you know, a witness in this case described you as the deputy of the Ilok Police Station in the fall of 1991. Was that -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formally and legally, I was never appointed the -- to the post of the deputy commander of the Ilok Police Station, although, internally, people would refer to me as one.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And why was that? What was it about your function which gave rise to that perception?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This all occurred in late 1991. The Serbian army formed its command headquarters within Ilok, and the town of Ilok was under military administration. Some of the forces, I believe it was upon orders by the deputy minister or the chief of the Department of Public Security, Mr. Stojkovic, some of the police forces of Serbia were sent to Ilok to establish a police station there. These were professionals who had fled from different regions of Republic of Croatia. Since I was at the very border of Republic of Croatia where the station of Ilok was located and had my check-points and patrols there, the staff assigned me with assisting the work of the Ilok Police Station, and my assistance there was of an advisory nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's request: Could extra microphones be turned off, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And who were you advising, and in which kind of circumstances? Let's try and break it down. How often, if at all, would you go to Ilok?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that period, quite often.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the station?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of Ilok station was Dusan Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And how well or badly organised was the Ilok station under Knezevic?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Why did you arrive at that view?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He got the police station to operate in the way they normally operate in Serbia, and I believe also in Croatia at the time, very quickly, with the basic task of law enforcement and crime prevention.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What kind of advice were you giving?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was there to help out, to provide a link between my police station, primarily my sector on the side where I was, and the police station in Backa Palanka with which Ilok was co-operating, and that co-operation had been good and close even earlier because only a river divided these two towns. They had the same security situation. So that communication was necessary; it was established. The communication system was to be set up, along with the records that every police station is supposed to keep.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: From when do -- from when to when do you think you were entering Ilok and engaged in this kind of work, in relation to the Ilok Police Station?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From end 1991, more precisely, November or December, I can't remember exactly, until mid-1992, when, following a decision of the staff, I was transferred to Hrtkovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you move around Ilok, or did you simply attend the police station during this period?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I moved around.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you observe any training base in Ilok during that period?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Ilok? No. Ilok was under military administration, under military rule, and the military had all the powers.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What's the significance of that, if at all, that the military had the rule and they had all the powers? What's the significance in relation to my question as to whether there was a training base?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the military command co-ordinated the work of both the police and the army and the businesses, the economy in Ilok. And all the activities were subordinated to the command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just try to get things on the right track. What Mr. Jordash is asking you is that, even if that's true what you tell us, what does that mean in terms of being able to see a training centre, a training base? I mean, and I think that that's Mr. Jordash's problem, that even if there's military rule in that area, that does not prevent a training base to be there. So, therefore, the answer is difficult to understand. The answer is a very factual -- the question is a very factual one: Did you see any training base, irrespective of who was commanding the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not in Ilok.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you hear of any training base in Ilok?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say "not in Ilok," where, then, you have seen a training base at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time, I did not see a training base in Ilok or around Ilok.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know if the military were conducting any training in the Eastern Slavonian region or in the wider region?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the wider region ... I did not understand. The wider region of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, let's stick with Eastern Slavonia. Do you know if the military were conducting any training at that time, late 1991/early 1992, in Eastern Slavonia. If you don't know, it's fine to say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know if there was any training being conducted within Serbia by the military, by the JNA at that time?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you meet anyone by the name Bozovic at the time you were working, entering into Ilok?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In which circumstances?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him in Ilok. I saw him perhaps two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know if he was engaged in any work in Ilok or the surrounding areas?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not engaged in Ilok, not on the Ilok police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know if he was engaged anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to go to or observe anything happening at Pajzos?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, I was at Pajzos perhaps two or three times. It was, generally speaking, an area where we didn't go. And when I say "we," I mean us from the police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, would you allow me to go back to the previous line of questioning. You said you met Mr. Bozovic two or three times. Was this a professional meeting or an occasional private meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We met around town, but not professionally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So is this to say that it was just for a cup of coffee or just meeting each other on the street by incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We met in passing. I can't be sure whether we met once at the police station, whether he ever came to the police station. In Ilok.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you know what his -- how did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I was told by the commander of the police station who he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what did the commander tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe, if I can remember well now, that he was then at Pajzos. He was based at Pajzos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Doing what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you mean by "Pajzos"? Just a location? Was he a farmer there? Was he ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. When I saw him, he was in uniform. And Pajzos is a location where there was a building, a villa, and a couple of auxiliary buildings that were used to store agricultural machinery. And there was a winery as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what's the link between uniforms and agriculture and machinery? I mean, was there anything else, apart from the winery and the storage of agricultural machinery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there were reports at the time, at the time, that there was some sort of communications centre or a relay centre up there. And it sounded believable, because that location is actually on a higher ground. It dominates over the surrounding area. I think he was associated to that communications centre, but I didn't go up there. I've never seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I take you back to one of the previous questions by Mr. Jordash. You answered one of his question that he was not engaged in Ilok, not on the Ilok police force. Then the question was: Do you know if he was engaged anywhere else? Your answer was: "I don't know." The answer should have been: I was informed that he was linked to the Pajzos location where, as I learned, there was a communications centre, and he was wearing a uniform. Witness DST-040, to tell us about the winery and the agricultural machinery, where it should be perfectly clear to you that we're not primarily interested in wine-making but, rather, in performing functions on different matters, would you please answer the questions right away, focussing on what is perfectly clear to you, the focus of this Tribunal, and that is: Military and/or police activity. Is it clear to you that you were not giving the details of what you knew about the person you were asked about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I met Bozovic and met him around in Ilok.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm talking about the question put to you by Mr. Jordash, what you would know about his engagement. And I'm also asking -- I'm also referring to my question to you, what Pajzos was. If you know that it's -- at least that you were told that it's a communications centre, which sounded logical to you, because it was at a higher elevation, then I'm not primarily, although you may add that, interested in wine-making and agricultural machinery. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then please behave in accordance with what I just brought to your attention. Mr. Jordash, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What kind of uniform was Bozovic wearing?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform. I think it was some kind of NATO uniform. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you hear or observe any kind of training base at Pajzos at that time?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never noticed any.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's go to paragraph 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, again, the -- perhaps it's my understanding of the English language. "I never noticed." That seems to refer to what the witness observed. Your question was, rather, whether he heard or observed. Did you ever hear about a training centre in Pajzos, even if you did not have personally observed it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I never heard there was any kind of training base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have 1D02630, please, on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is D415, MFI, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Have you seen this before, Mr. Witness; and do you recognise the facts that are stated within?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've not seen the document, but I recognise the facts contained therein.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you at any stage attend the training at Tara, whether to be trained or as a trainer, or in any other capacity?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In relation to the mention there of assigning officers as instructors --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to apologise. It's me now. My mobile can be seized by anyone who has an interest in doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Or who dare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll switch it off.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So, Mr. Witness, in relation to the mention in the document of assigning officers as instructors who preferably meet the following conditions that: "They are assigned to the PJM, exceptionally assigned officers outside of the PJM, that they are finished Military Academy or are reserve officers, young, psychologically stable, able to demonstrate specific acts and actions, and train others in the acquired knowledge and skills." Do you know anything about that instruction?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know because in 1993 I was the deputy detachment commander based in Novi Sad. And I can see that this dispatch was sent to all SUPs in the territory of the Republic of Serbia, as well as to the Pristina staff. I can also see that they were supposed to designate officers from their institutions that would be sent for training at Tara. And I can see that the then-MUP staff was based in Bajina Basta. As officers, we acted on such dispatches, and we sent officers to the collection point defined in such dispatches.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Where was the collection point?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The collection point was Tara. You can read that in the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And how were the trainers, the instructors, selected? Who were they?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trainers belonged to the PJM detachments. Each detachment selected detachment commanders, platoon commanders, instructors among those who were fit, who had mostly graduated from military academies. That was one way of educating highly trained police officers. They also selected them from the ranks of reserve forces, which meant that they possessed knowledge and skills required to carry out military and police training.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: At that time at Tara, early 1993, was there anybody outside of the public security conducting the training of the PJM?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who was running, or who was the overall commander of the training at Tara at that time?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who the commander was, but Obrad Stevanovic was the PJM commander. I don't know whether he appointed somebody else besides himself. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And Obrad Stevanovic reported to Stojicic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know who Stojicic reported to?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was only logical that he would report to the Ministry of the Interior, to -- because he was his subordinate.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, there's been evidence in this case, Mr. Witness, that the Serbian DB were conducting or running training bases in a number of places around 1991, 1992, and through to 1995. But sticking with 1991, 1992, and 1993, did anyone suggest to you, or did you hear any suggestion, that the PJM should be sent to any DB training base at that time they were being sent to the Tara for training?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: PJM detachments were deployed and they took turns along the entire length of the border on the Drina. And they were deployed at several locations. I don't know if they were trained and how extensively.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think you've maybe misunderstood my question. Did you ever hear a suggestion, or was a suggestion made to you, in 1993 that instead of sending PJM to Tara for training, they should be sent to any DB training base.

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We implemented what we received in the dispatches.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What kind of training did they receive at Tara; and what was the primary purpose of the training? What was it supposed to achieve?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the plan for training was prescribed and issued by the PJM commander. That training plan was submitted to all PJM detachments in the territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter kindly asks that all computers that are not in use please be switched off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] PJM detachments then elaborated those training plans, and the training plan contained both training in shooting and arms, physical training, orientation in -- and moving in space, setting up ambushes, training aimed at curbing public disorder, and how to act in situations when there are major disturbances of public peace and order. Training in securing public buildings and public areas. And that was all part of PJM activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Had the Serbian police or the Vojvodina police received this kind of training before; or was this something completely new?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of that training had existed beforehand, but things were changed due to the newly arisen security situation. Therefore, there were more activities with regard to the protection of the state border.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And after the PJM had been trained, are you able to explain, very briefly, where the detachments were deployed?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They returned to their base units.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And where were their base units then deployed? How were these new skills utilized?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The newly acquired skills were utilized in activities which those professionals applied in their police stations, and they were immediately involved in regular policing duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, perhaps I should have been more specific. Which locations are we referencing here? Which locations were these police stations in?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about their base units. In other words, police stations were distributed across the territories of the detachments. To be more specific, the detachment in Novi Sad was composed of men from the police stations from all over the territory of the province of Vojvodina, Subotica, Sombor, Novi Sad, Mitrovica, and Pancevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour would, it be possible to take a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's time for a break. We'll take the break, and we'll resume at a quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we just quickly have on the screen, before I return to this document on the screen, P442. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we just go to the bottom of the English, please. Actually, I think I'd like a different document. May we take the break at this point and I'll find that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take the break at this point and resume --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, before you continue: A meeting will take place next week between the Registry and the Dutch authorities. That was planned already. The medical condition of Mr. Stanisic, most likely supported by a brief report by Dr. Falke, will be put on the agenda and will be discussed during that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Before the break, we were going to look at this decision, and I do want to look at this decision. It's signed and accepted that it's signed by Stanisic. Now, we've heard how the procedure occurred in practice, and I want to just ask you, since we're on this subject, how it actually happened, if you can recall, in relation to this man. Do you recall this man? You've indicated in your statement at paragraph 43 he was a member of the JATD. Do you recall how his employment occurred and what involvement, if any, Mr. Stanisic had, other than signing the document?

utterances.speaker: DST-040 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We can't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that for technical --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The microphone is off. Then ... Yes, could you please re-start your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember the name. I believe that he had arrived from Pancevo. He had the recommendation of the Pancevo centre's chief, and he was admitted as a candidate, first in the ranks of the reserves, and then in the ranks of the active force. Later on, I believe that he was a member of the JSO. He had undergone training. I believe that for a while he worked with a group of people on the escort detail. I believe that for a while he was one of the Mr. Jovica Stanisic's escorts. The chief of service didn't know anything about the procedure by way of which the candidate was admitted. He only put his signature on the document, which was a standard procedure. He put his signature on all such documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness DST-040, have you followed -- no, could you please ... You have not followed the discussions, but there some material which the Defence might want to put to you in the continuation of your examination. That is still very uncertain. If you will receive a specific request, perhaps with a few questions or at least a package of material, with the invitation to review that material, then, you may do so. And if the request is just whether you were to review it, please do so without discussing it with anyone. If any party would like to communicate with you, the Chamber will then, through the channel of VWS, send you a message about what you are supposed to do. And if there's any request for writing down any comments as you deem fit and then return that to the address from where the -- from where you received the request, you are allowed to do that. You are, however, not allowed to discuss with anyone else or to communicate with anyone else about your testimony. Is that clear? If you are in any doubt as to what you're allowed to do or what you're not allowed to do, please put any question in that respect through the Victims and Witness Section so that the Chamber will respond to such a question. Is there anything the parties would like to add to what I just said to the witness? I see that there's no such request. Then would you please follow the usher. And we'd like to see you back in a little bit over one month.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We are about to adjourn. Since we are now in open session, I'd like to clearly state on behalf of the Chamber that we're trying to do our utmost best to see whether the public character of this trial can be better served, and we're working on it so that we may hear more of the evidence in open session rather than in closed session. We adjourn. And we'll resume on the 4th of October, a Tuesday, at quarter past 2.00 in this same courtroom, II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
